content.title: Masters 2026 live updates: Rory McIlroy wins second straight Masters
content.text: 10d ago / 7:25 PM EDTRory McIlroy wins despite 'tough weekend'McIlroy said the way he battled to close out a win Sunday felt similar to last year. Both then and today, he shot a double-bogey early in the round and had to regain his nerves and lead."I looked at the (score)board after I made the bogey on on six, and I think I went back to 9-under at that point," McIlroy said on CBS in his post-round interview from Butler Cabin. "I said, OK, if I can get to 14-under, I think I've got a really good chance of winning this tournament."He did, as a repeat winner."I just can’t believe I waited 17 years to get one green jacket, and I get two in a row," McIlroy said. "I think all of my my perseverance at this golf tournament over the years has really started to pay off. It was a tough weekend. I did the bulk of my work on on Thursday and Friday, but just so, so happy to hang in there and get the job done."10d ago / 7:21 PM EDTRory McIlroy: 'Incredible' to win with his mom, dad both presentMcIlroy won the Masters last year but neither of his parents was able to make the trip to Georgia. They almost didn't want to attend this year, either, he told CBS after the round."There was a piece of them that didn't want to come this year because they thought, 'OK, we didn't come last year, maybe that was the reason,'" McIlroy told CBS. "But I'm so glad that they got to experience this today. I'm going to, you know, we're all going to have a great time tonight."10d ago / 6:55 PM EDTRory McIlroy wins the Masters!McIlroy bogeyed on 18, but with a two-stroke lead, that was enough for Rory to win his second straight Masters.Scottie Scheffler finished second at 11-under. 10d ago / 6:52 PM EDTRory McIlroy recovers, needs two putts to win McIlroy's shot from left of the fairway found the bunker, but he was able to chip it up and past the hole to a makeable distance. McIlroy will have two putts to win the green jacket for a second consecutive year.10d ago / 6:47 PM EDTWatch: Rory McIlroy's tee shot on 18 goes far off fairwayDon't give McIlroy a second green jacket just yet. His tee shot off the final hole of his round has gone wide off the fairway to the left and left him with a difficult lie. He has a two-shot lead.10d ago / 6:39 PM EDTRory McIlroy nearly chips in on 17th holeMcIlroy has a commanding lead of this tournament with one hole to go.On the 17th and penultimate hole, McIlroy nearly chipped in from just off the green and tapped in for par to stay at 13-under. He has a two-shot lead entering the tournament's 72nd hole. Can he become the fourth player ever to win consecutive tournaments?10d ago / 6:37 PM EDTJustin Rose finishes 10 under, tied for thirdRose held the lead entering the back nine but bogeys on the 11th, 12th and 17th holes doomed his chance at a first green jacket. He finishes with a 2-under round of 70. It's his fifth time finishing the Masters in the top five. 10d ago / 6:30 PM EDTA reminder on back-to-back Masters winnersRory McIlroy is looking to join a group that includes...Jack Nicklaus, who won consecutive Masters in 1965 and 1966Nick Faldo, who did so in 1989 and 1990And Tiger Woods, the golfer who most recently won two straight at Augusta in 2001 and 2002.10d ago / 6:29 PM EDTWatch: Rory's sensational putt at 16 maintains his leadMcIlroy put his first putt within inches by brilliantly reading the green's slope. 10d ago / 6:22 PM EDTScottie Scheffler finishes at 11-underScheffler played bogey-free golf the last two rounds — actually, his bogey-free streak began on the 15th hole Friday — and finishes Sunday with a 4-under 68. That puts him at 11-under for the tournament. Scheffler now must hope for McIlroy to drop two strokes and force a playoff.Scheffler became the first player to go bogey-free in the third and final rounds of the Masters since 1942.10d ago / 6:10 PM EDTJustin Rose catches a huge breakHis tee shot on the 17th hole drifted wide ride into the trees, but caught a remarkable bounce off a tree and landed in the fairway. Just like he'd planned it all along, right?Rose is currently 11-under, two shots back of Rory McIlroy.10d ago / 6:07 PM EDTScheffler will enter final hole trailing McIlroy by two strokesScottie Scheffler was barely an inch away from sinking a birdie on the 17th hole, but his putt brushed past the hole, unwilling to drop. The world's top-ranked golfer made par, keeping him at 11-under with just one hole to go. He's still chasing leader Rory McIlroy (13-under). 10d ago / 5:59 PM EDTCurrent leaderboardRory McIlroy, -13 through 14 holesT-2nd: Scottie Scheffler (through 16), Justin Rose (through 15), -11T-4th: Tyrrell Hatton (66), Russell Henley (through 17), Cameron Young (through 14), -1010d ago / 5:56 PM EDTPar for Rory on No. 14Rory’s birdie streak ends at two, as he makes par on No. 14. He’s still in first with four holes to go, though Scottie Scheffler and Justin Rose are staying close.Cameron Young is three strokes behind McIlroy at 10-under after his birdie putt on 14 just missed. 10d ago / 5:54 PM EDTHere comes Scottie SchefflerScheffler had been part of a logjam at 10-under with five other players until the 16th hole, when he dropped in a birdie to improve to 11-under, two shots behind leader Rory McIlroy. 10d ago / 5:46 PM EDTSam Burns, Scottie Scheffler making a last push for the leadSam Burns has birdied his last two holes, as Nos. 13 and 14, to move to 9-under. He's trying to overcome his dreadful start to the final round that saw him double-bogey and bogey the second and third holes. Scheffler, meanwhile, has gained a stroke and is now 10-under through 15 holes after a birdie that left the gallery of patron roaring. It will take quite a close for either to touch Rory McIlroy, however, with the way the defending champion has recovered to take a three-shot lead at 13-under.10d ago / 5:45 PM EDTMassive birdie from Rory on No. 13That’s back-to-back birdies from McIlroy, who now holds a three-stroke lead over second at 13-under. He’s pulling away from Cameron Young, who hasn’t birdied since the eighth hole. 10d ago / 5:35 PM EDTQuite a performance by Collin MorikawaBack in February, when he won the Pebble Beach Pro-Am, Collin Morikawa might have been a favorite to win the Masters, but he arrived in Augusta this week just trying to physically endure four rounds of golf because of a back injury that led him to withdraw from the Players Championship in early March. He said this week he was taking his health "day by day."Despite back pain, Morikawa birdied five holes in a row, starting with No. 12, in his final round Sunday, and entering the 18th hole sits at 9-under and tied for sixth, just three shots off the lead.10d ago / 5:28 PM EDTBrutal stretch for Justin RoseAfter a bogey on both the 11th and 12 holes to move him out of the lead and back to 10-under, Justin Rose had an opportunity for eagle on No. 13. An eagle would move him into a tie for the lead with Rory McIlroy at 12-under.Instead, Rose missed his putts for both eagle and birdie, and finds himself now two shots back of the lead with precious little time to make up ground. Rose was so bothered by missed opportunity that before he left the 13th green, he turned and took one last look. 10d ago / 5:23 PM EDTHuge birdie for Rory McIlroy on No. 12And now Rory is finding a rhythm. He’s at 12-under par after a birdie on No. 12. Cameron Young made par, keeping him at 10-under.McIlroy is in first place with six holes to go. 10d ago / 5:22 PM EDTRussell Henley misses a putt to tie for leadThe Georgia native just missed a birdie opportunity on the 15th hole. Instead of pushing him to 11-under and a share of the lead, Henley will remain at 10-under. 10d ago / 5:14 PM EDTTyrrell Hatton finishes with a 66The English golfer finishes at 10-under after carding a 6-under 66 Sunday that included an eagle from the fairway on the seventh hole, but also bogeys on No. 4 and No. 10. He'll be watching, perhaps from the driving range, to see whether any extra holes will be needed to decide this tournament.10d ago / 5:12 PM EDTAnother par for Rory on No. 11That’s three straight pars for Rory, who is in the lead at 11-under through 11 holes.Cameron Young also made par, and he’s tied with three other golfers in second.10d ago / 5:04 PM EDTA nightmare for Justin Rose on 12The co-leader, Rose was trying to chip onto the 12th green when he duffed the shot, hitting it only a few yards, which left him still short of the green. He finished the hole with a bogey to fall to 10-under and is now one shot behind the leader, Rory McIlroy.10d ago / 4:55 PM EDTYoung, McIlroy start back nine with a par Rory McIlroy and Cam Young both made par on No. 10.Rory is tied with Justin Rose for first place, while Young is tied with two others in second at 10-under. 10d ago / 4:51 PM EDTOn No. 11, Justin Rose drops a stroke Rose has bogeyed the 11th hole to go 11-under, and slide into a tie for first with Rory McIlroy. 10d ago / 4:42 PM EDTDisappointing par for Rory on No. 9McIlroy had a great chance at a birdie, but his putt wouldn’t drop. He remains one stroke behind Justin Rose for the lead. Cameron Young, meanwhile, bogeyed No. 9, dropping him into a tie for third place at 10-under. 10d ago / 4:29 PM EDTYoung, McIlroy both birdie No. 8That’s back-to-back birdies for Rory, who has recovered nicely after some bogey troubles.He and Cameron Young are both at 11-under par, one shot behind Justin Rose for the lead. 10d ago / 4:27 PM EDTA fifth player is now double-digits under parWith a birdie on the 16th hole, Tyrell Hatton has moved to 10-under, joining him for the moment with Rory McIlroy, Russell Henley and Cameron Young in a tie for second. With just two holes left in his round Hatton has much less time to make up more ground, however.10d ago / 4:20 PM EDTCan Justin Rose finally break through?Rose is having a fantastic final round so far, shooting 3-under par through the front nine.This is not the first time Rose has surged on Augusta’s final day. Last year, he shot a 66 to force a playoff against Rory McIlroy.Rose has lost in a Masters playoff twice — joining Ben Hogan as the only golfer with that bittersweet distinction. Is today the day Rose finally holds on for a win? 10d ago / 4:18 PM EDTThird straight birdie gives Rose two-shot lead Justin Rose has moved to 12-under after a birdie on the ninth hole. He's two shots ahead of Rory McIlroy, Cameron Young and Russell Henley who sit at 10-under currently. Rose, 45, is trying to become the second-oldest Masters champion.10d ago / 4:10 PM EDTA much-needed birdie for Rory McIlroyRory birdies on No. 7, moving him back into a tie for second with Cameron Young and Russell Henley. They trail Justin Rose by one stroke. 10d ago / 4:09 PM EDTJustin Rose has found an opening to winWhat a final round we have unfolding. As Rory McIlroy battles to regain his place atop the leaderboard, the player he defeated last year to win this tournament, Justin Rose, moved into a tie for first at 11-under with Cameron Young.Rose shot a birdie on the par-5 eighth hole to get two straight birdies. His only miscue today was a bogey on the third hole.Just minutes after his birdie putt rolled in, Rose was the outright leader after Young shot a bogey.10d ago / 4:09 PM EDTA bogey for Cameron Young on No. 7Young got stuck in the bunker on the seventh hole, and left his putt for par short. His bogey drops him to 10-under — and into second place. 10d ago / 4:01 PM EDTWho is Russell Henley, currently in second place?This is the 10th Masters in the career of Russell Henley, but unlike names like Justin Rose, Rory McIlroy and Scottie Scheffler that surround him on the scoreboard, Henley isn't a household name. A win today would change that. Henley, who is currently 10-under and tied for second with Rose, a stroke behind Cameron Young, is a 37-year-old Georgia native who played collegiately at Georgia. He has been game in major championships before, finishing top-10 in both the U.S. and British Opens.Henley put himself in contention this week with a second-round, 6-under 66. In the final round, he's birdied four holes so far through nine holes. Not bad for someone who describes himself as "never really that calm.""I might look like it, but I’m never really that calm," he told reporters after his second round. "I’m a pretty nervous person. [Thurday] just was terrible. It was such a tough day. Really stunk to start out my first day like that."I really wanted to come play well today. I knew I could do it, so hopefully it’s good enough to play the weekend."10d ago / 3:55 PM EDTAnother bogey for Rory McIlroyUh oh. Rory struggles on another Par 3, this time making a bogey on No. 6. McIlroy is at 9-under through six holes, tied with Scottie Scheffler for fourth place. Cameron Young also bogeyed on No. 7, bringing him to 11-under. He has a one stroke lead over second place. 10d ago / 3:43 PM EDTMcIlroy, Young make par on No. 5Young is still in first place, leading three golfers — including Rory — by two strokes. 10d ago / 3:41 PM EDTJustin Rose now in second as wellRose miraculously came out of the dirt to make a birdie on No. 7, and now he’s 10-under, two shots behind Cameron Young for first place. 10d ago / 3:38 PM EDTRussell Henley moves into a tie for secondA birdie on No. 8 puts Henley at 10-under, tied with Rory McIlroy for second. 10d ago / 3:27 PM EDTA missed opportunity for Justin RoseOn the par-3 sixth hole, last year's Masters runner-up Justin Rose had a putt for birdie that would have moved him to 10-under and tied with Rory McIlroy for second. But instead of becoming only the third player at double-digit under par, Rose pushed the putt to the right, and ended with par. He stays at 9-under.10d ago / 3:25 PM EDTDisaster for Rory McIlroy on No. 4Rory missed multiple putts on No. 4, and ended up with a double bogey on the par-3 hole. Cameron Young made par, and he now has a two-shot lead at 12-under par headed into No. 5. 10d ago / 3:17 PM EDTThe fifth hole has been this tournament's most difficultWith the final pairing of Rory McIlroy and Cameron Young about to tee off on the fourth hole, they're approaching what has been the most difficult hole on the course during the Masters — the 495-yard, par-4 fifth. Players have shot an average of 4.3 strokes there this week, making it the hardest, relative to par, on the course. The contour of the green makes it especially challenging.10d ago / 3:11 PM EDTClutch birdie from Rory McIlroy on No. 3Rory is back into a tie for first at 12-under par after a birdie putt on the third hole.After missing his own chance for a birdie, Cameron Young made par to keep pace with McIlroy. 10d ago / 3:09 PM EDTScottie Scheffler, a two-time champion, is lurking Scheffler started today three shots behind the leaders and after a birdie on the fourth hole is still three shots back from leader Cameron Young. Golf is a psychological sport, and with Rory McIlroy trying to avoid a collapse, and Cameron Young in the white-hot spotlight of Masters Sunday for the first time, don't count out Scheffler, who knows what it's like to close out a win on this course.10d ago / 2:59 PM EDTAnd Cameron Young takes the leadYoung is now in first place after a birdie on No. 2, while Rory McIlroy made par on the same hole, just missing his birdie putt. 10d ago / 2:55 PM EDTSam Burns double-bogeys second hole, drops out of leadBurns is having a rough start to his final round. He briefly pulled into a tie for the lead with Rory McIlroy and Cameron Young, after carding a birdie on the first hole. But he recorded a double-bogey the second hole to fall back.10d ago / 2:40 PM EDTPar for Rory on No. 1He stays at 11-under, tied with Cameron Young and Sam Burns for the lead. 10d ago / 2:31 PM EDTHow far under par will it take to win?Rory McIlroy and Cameron Young enter the final round sitting at 11-under par. History suggests they will need to stay in in the double-digits under par to win, as each of the last eight champions finished 10-under or better. Recent winners have finished:2025: Rory McIlroy, -112024: Scottie Scheffler, -112023: Jon Rahm, -122022: Scottie Scheffler, -102021: Hideki Matsuyama, -102020: Dustin Johnson, -202019: Tiger Woods, -132018: Patrick Reed, -152017: Sergio Garcia, -92016: Danny Willett, -52015: Jordan Spieth, -1810d ago / 2:29 PM EDTSam Burns grabs a share of the leadBurns joins Rory McIlroy and Cameron Young at 11-under after a birdie on hole one. 10d ago / 2:27 PM EDTThe final group is underway!Cameron Young and Rory McIlroy just teed off from the first hole.They both enter the day 11-under par, and start their final round with a one-shot lead over Sam Burns. 10d ago / 2:25 PM EDTKeegan Bradley was one of the day's early winnersFrom starting his final round at 3-over, Bradley finished at 3-under after birdies on four of his last six holes. A score like that won't put Bradley in contention for likely even the top 10, barring some collapses from the later pairings, but just like the birdie-filled rounds by Gary Woodland and Viktor Hovland, who fired rounds of 66 and 67, Bradley's 18 holes showed the rest of the field that this course can facilitate low scores today.10d ago / 2:15 PM EDTA reminder of what’s at stake on SundayThis year’s Masters purse is worth $22.5 million, an $1.5 million increase from last year.The winner will receive $4.5 million, second place will win $2.43 million, third place will receive $1.53 million and fourth place will win $1.08 million. The rest of the finishers will receiver under $1 million. Whoever finishes 50th — or last — will win $56,700. 10d ago / 2:05 PM EDTRory McIlroy would have good company if he losesRory McIlroy blowing a six-stroke lead after 36 holes is quite shocking, but also not a completely unique happenstance at Augusta.In 1996, two-time major winner Greg Norman had a six-stroke lead entering Sunday, and lost his lead over the course of the final round, ultimately finishing second to Nick Faldo.10d ago / 1:54 PM EDTA brief history of Rory McIlroy meltdownsUnfortunately for Rory McIlroy, blowing a six-stroke lead at the Masters is not completely shocking. The golfer has a history of poor finishes in majors, including...In 2011, McIlroy famously led by three shots headed into the back nine, but starting with the 10th hole he went triple bogey, bogey and double bogey to lose the lead.In 2018, McIlroy was seven-under in the third round, but was nine shots worse Sunday when he was in the final pairing with Patrick Reed.In 2024, McIlroy had a two-stroke lead over Bryson DeChambeau with four holes to play at the U.S. Open, but bogeyed three of the remaining holes to finish in second. 10d ago / 1:46 PM EDTNo low amateur, againWhat started as a field with six amateurs was trimmed to zero after all shot worse than 4-over par through 36 holes and missed the cut. It's the second consecutive year that no amateurs have made the weekend at the Masters. It means that no amateur will be invited to Butler Cabin at the tournament's finale to join the Masters champion in his green-jacket celebration, and no amateur will win the "silver cup," given to the low amateur.10d ago / 1:37 PM EDTKeep an eye on Justin Rose...Rose, the ninth-ranked golfer in the world, enters Sunday three strokes behind first place.Last year, Rose was seven shots behind Rory McIlroy entering the final round, and made up the deficit to force a playoff, which Rose ultimately lost.Rose has a flair for the dramatic at Augusta. He’s finished second three times, and he’s one of only two golfers (along with Ben Hogan) to lose two playoffs at the Masters. 10d ago / 1:23 PM EDTWatch: Cameron Young fires 65 to tie for lead after 54 holesYoung had eight birdies, plus a bogey, to move up into the co-leader position.10d ago / 1:20 PM EDTViktor Hovland is on a final-round tearBy starting the day at 1-over, Viktor Hovland was among the earliest to tee off Sunday, but he's shown what is possible on the course today after firing seven birdies through his first 13 holes. He stands at 6-under currently.10d ago / 1:12 PM EDTMcIlroy trying to join an exclusive club of repeat winnersAfter winning the Masters in 2025, Rory McIlroy was back in the lead after the first round. But staying in contention is difficult, even for past champions, as Masters history shows. Only three previous winners have ever defended their titles by winning a second consecutive green jacket. Jack Nicklaus did it in 1965-66, Nick Faldo in 1989-90, and the last was Tiger Woods, in 2001-02. "If you’re going to win two years in a row, you’ll find conditions you like and maybe you don’t find conditions you like, but you’ve got to adjust to both of those," Nicklaus told reporters this week. "I think Rory is talented enough to be able to play it. Rory’s got the monkey off his back, and I think he has a very, very good chance to repeat."To Nicklaus's point, after McIlroy's opening round he said that having won last year allowed him to play more freely."I said this when I came in on Tuesday, I think winning a Masters makes it easier to win your second one. I do," McIlroy told reporters. "It’s hard to say because there’s still shots out there that you feel a little bit tight with, and you just have to stand up and commit to making a good swing and not worry about really where it goes."I think it’s easier for me to make those swings and not worry about where it goes when I know that I can go to the Champions Locker Room and put my green jacket on and have a Coke Zero at the end of the day."10d ago / 1:00 PM EDTGolf legends on 'the critical hole on the golf course'After teeing off from the first hole at Augusta National on Thursday as the honorary starters of the Masters, Tom Watson, Gary Player and Jack Nicklaus held a joint news conference to field questions about the state of the game. One question concerned the state of this course, specifically, whether they would change one hole if they could."I’d fill in the creek in front of No. 12," Watson said to laughs from reporters.That creek, of course, is Rae's Creek, the little body of water that has played a big role in the outcome of past tournaments."Good move," Nicklaus replied."That’s the critical hole on the golf course, to be honest with you, and I think everybody in this room understands that," said Watson, who had hit balls into the creek "too many times."But the conversation quickly became a discussion of the hole, its history and how to play it. Let's pick up the back-and-forth here.GARY PLAYER: "It’s a great example for golf architects to realize you don’t have to make the holes all that long. That’s an 8-iron, and it’s crippled more people than polio. This hole, it’s really some hole. The most miracle of all time, when Fred Couples stuck on the bank. If you think of everybody, look what happened when Tiger won the last time. Three guys came along with double bogeys."And how about Jordan Spieth?"TOM WATSON: "It’s a great hole."GARY PLAYER: "Jordan Spieth might have hurt his career, a 70. He might have had a four- or five-shot lead going into that hole. I think the secret of that hole is always to -- funny enough, Bobby Jones said this to me, make your pin at the back of the green, and there’s a lot of merit to that."I knocked it in the hole from the bunker one year. You can’t knock it in from the water unless you’ve got a helluva underwater stroke."10d ago / 12:45 PM EDTWatch: Shane Lowry's Saturday hole-in-oneLowry's hole-in-one Saturday was the first at the Masters since 2022, and only the seventh to occur all-time on the par-3 sixth hole. Remarkably, this wasn't Lowry's first ace at the Masters. He also made one in 2016, on the 16th hole. In all, this was the fifth hole-in-one of his career."It gives you obviously a huge kind of boost,” Lowry told reporters. "You go from 6-under to 8-under, and then all of a sudden, you’re only four back. It’s getting real now."10d ago / 12:28 PM EDTWhat Rory McIlroy had to say after his disastrous third roundHere is some of what McIlroy said to reporters in a press conference following his 1-over par third round, which eliminated the six-stroke lead he had headed into Saturday.On his overall play in the third round: “This golf course has a way of, when you’re not quite feeling it, you struggle. You have to dig deep.”On his plan for Sunday: “I’d like to think that I’ll play a little bit freer and I’ll play, you know, like I’ve already got a green jacket, which I do. Sometimes I just have to remind myself of that. I wish I was a few shots better off, but I’m comfortable. ... I just know I need to be better tomorrow to have a chance.”10d ago / 12:14 PM EDTWhat to know about Cameron YoungYoung shot a 7-under third round to move into a first-place tie with Rory McIlroy headed into the final round. Here’s what to know about Young...In 2021-22, Young was named the PGA Tour Rookie of the Year, finishing as the runner-up in five tournaments that season.Young has won only two tournaments in his PGA Tour career.Young is currently the third-ranked player on the Tour.Young’s best finish at the Masters is seventh, which he did in 2023. His best finish at a major is second, which he achieved at the 2022 Open Championship. 10d ago / 11:49 AM EDTThird-round recapAfter torching the course to end the second round, Rory McIlroy didn't get under par again until the 10th hole of his third round, and finished 1-over for the day, standing at 11-under. "I have to look at the positives, even though there aren’t that many to take today," McIlroy told reporters. "I did bounce back. I hit some good shots coming in. I’m in a great position. I just know I need to be better tomorrow to have a chance."That slower start allowed the rest of the field to cut into what had been a 6-shot lead to start the day. The day's biggest mover was Cameron Young, whose eight birdies led to a 65 that has him now tied for first with McIlroy. They will tee off at 2:25 p.m. ET in Sunday's final pairing. For Young, it's an incredible rebound considering he started the tournament 4-over — through his first seven holes. He has finished in the top-10 at the Masters in two of the last three years, so he's played well on the course. But the pressure of a Masters Sunday is a different animal.One shot behind the co-leaders is Sam Burns, who has been hanging around the lead since the very first day.10d ago / 11:40 AM EDTMind your Masters mannersAccording to The Scotsman, Scottish player Robert MacIntyre was reprimanded by Augusta National officials for his behavior following his opening-round 80 Thursday. MacIntyre was caught on camera flipping a middle finger toward the 15th hole amid his quadruple bogey there.10d ago / 11:19 AM EDTWhy is Bryson DeChambeau not playing today?Including ties, the top 50 players after the second round make the cut at the Masters. Inevitably, that cut line — which stood at 4-over this year — leaves several notable players left out. This year, those who did not make the weekend were highlighted by Bryson DeChambeau, the 2020 and 2024 U.S. Open champion. Others left out:Danny Willett, 2016 Masters championMike Weir, 2003 Masters championJ.J. Spaun, the 2025 U.S. Open champion, who had won a PGA Tour event earlier this monthZach Johnson, the 2007 Masters and 2015 British Open championBubba Watson, the 2012 and 2014 Masters championAkshay Bhatia, who had matched the cut line with a chip-in birdie on the penultimate hole Friday, only to double-bogey the 18th and final hole of his second round, and miss the cut.10d ago / 10:56 AM EDTIn second round, a long streak came to an end When two-time Masters champion Scottie Scheffler shot a 2-over 74 in Friday's second round, it ended his streak of 11 consecutive rounds at par or better at this tournament. That streak tied Scheffler, who has never finished outside the top 20 at the Masters, for third-longest all-time.10d ago / 10:56 AM EDTSecond-round recapMcIlroy started in the lead at 6-under but two bogeys dropped him to 4-under through 10 holes. That kick-started a hellacious stretch that saw him birdie six of the next eight holes to finish with a round of 66, and move to 12-under for the tournament. It gave McIlroy a six-shot lead over Patrick Reed and Sam Burns, the largest lead through 36 holes in Masters history. McIlroy built his lead with excellent putting, averaging 1.42 putts per hole through the second round, which was ahead of the 1.67 average of the field.10d ago / 10:55 AM EDTFirst-round recapDefending champion Rory McIlroy was tied for the lead after the first round after shooting a 5-under 67, his lowest opening round at the Masters in 15 years. Sam Burns, playing his fifth Masters, also shot a 67 thanks to shooting a combined 5-under on the course's four par-5 holes. Patrick Reed, who won the Masters in 2018, was two shots behind, while two-time Masters winner Scottie Scheffler — the world's No. 1-ranked golfer, was three shots behind the leaders.
